metaData.originalTitle: 电商搜索 H1 提升 AI-Coding 质量实践 RD & QA
metaData.title: Improving AI-Coding Quality in E-commerce Search: RD & QA Practices
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically elaborates on the practical framework and core conclusions for systematically improving the quality and controllability of AI-generated code in the e-commerce search domain, leveraging the Harness engineering infrastructure and a full-stack organizational model, combined with a three-layer constraint framework (input/generation/output).
metaData.summary: Based on the practices of Baidu's e-commerce search team, this article systematically explains how to systematically improve code quality in the era of AI-Coding. The core framework includes: Harness engineering as the infrastructure, full-stack capability as the organizational model, and three-layer constraints (input/generation/output) as the quality control mechanism. Through three progressive project cases (Brand Card iteration, List Automation, Outfit Assistant Agent), it demonstrates the application effects of this method across projects of varying complexity, including development cycle compression, testing efficiency improvement, and faster anomaly detection. The article also details the transformation of the RD and QA collaboration model, upgrading from linear handoff to closed-loop co-creation, with QA shifting left to the standard-setting phase and RD outputting standardized Specs, jointly achieving testing efficiency gains and delivery quality assurance. Finally, it outlines the expansion plans for the team and business levels going forward.

mainPoints.point: The core of AI-Coding quality management has shifted from 'whether to manage' to 'how to manage'.
mainPoints.explanation: When 80% of the code is generated by AI, quality control is no longer an option but a problem that must be systematically solved. The article proposes a framework of Harness engineering + full-stack capability + three-layer constraints.

mainPoints.point: Harness engineering is the infrastructure, and full-stack capability is the organizational model.
mainPoints.explanation: By establishing engineering constraints (such as workspace mode, TDD-driven development, audit verification) and organizational capabilities (one-person full-stack), it supports the new collaboration model between RD and QA, ensuring the safe deployment of AI-generated code.

mainPoints.point: The RD and QA collaboration model has upgraded from linear handoff to closed-loop co-creation.
mainPoints.explanation: QA shifts left to the standard-setting phase, RD outputs standardized Specs, and both parties form a closed-loop collaboration in requirements review, test case generation, bug localization, fix suggestions, and regression verification.

mainPoints.point: Three types of project practices validated the effectiveness of the method.
mainPoints.explanation: The Brand Card project saw a 20%+ reduction in cycle time and a 30% compression in testing cycles; the List project completed the full chain with 1 RD × 6 weeks; the Outfit Assistant Agent project established a complete observability and evaluation system.

mainPoints.point: The core of the Agent project is 'humans define standards, AI executes verification'.
mainPoints.explanation: It transforms experience-driven manual judgment into rule-driven automated AI verification, achieving quality control through platform capabilities like dialogue evaluation, prompt debugging, and full-chain tracing.

keyQuotes: Quality = Input Constraints × Generation Constraints × Output Constraints
Humans define standards, AI executes verification
Let AI-generated code go online safely, both sides are teammates

relatedArticles.title: Harness Engineering: How I Spent a Week Boosting AI Coding Rate to 90% in an Enterprise App
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically introduces Harness Engineering, a new AI coding paradigm that elevates the AI code rate of an enterprise Java application from 25% to over 90% by building a four-element system of rules, skills, knowledge, and change management.

relatedArticles.title: Investing 10,000 RMB in AI: A Year of Tools, Practices, and Reflections
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A systematic summary of a veteran developer's practical experience in the AI wave, covering everything from MAC toolchain optimization and Harness Engineering architectural constraints to building an Agent-driven automated learning loop.

relatedArticles.title: Browser Use: Building a Runtime Harness for Agents
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details how to build an open-source tool based on the Chrome DevTools Protocol that enables AI agents to operate real browsers for multi-dimensional verification—including visual, interactive, and console checks—thereby ensuring the delivery quality of web products.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Engineering: Enabling Coding Agents to Reliably Complete Long-Horizon Tasks
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article introduces the Harness Engineering framework, which addresses the reliability challenges of Coding Agents in large-scale, long-horizon tasks through task decomposition, parallel scheduling, File-as-Progress state persistence, and multi-layered retry mechanisms.

relatedArticles.title: The Evolution of Agent/Skills/Teams Architectures and Principles of Technology Selection
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically reviews the evolutionary trajectory of AI Agents from monolithic to multi-agent, then to Skills pluginization and Teams parallel collaboration, and, drawing on the latest research from Google and Anthropic, provides a scientific methodology for selection.

relatedArticles.title: AI R&D Automation: Wiki Knowledge Base + Skill Pack
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details how to build a continuously growing team knowledge base and a supporting expert skill pack based on the LLM-Wiki model and the Obsidian platform to achieve AI-driven R&D automation.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Is Not the Goal, Knowledge Is the Moat — Knowledge Accumulation Practices of an AI Engineering Delivery Team
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the engineering delivery practices of an AI Team, this article proposes that knowledge accumulation is more important than workflow orchestration, and systematically introduces a complete methodology encompassing a five-layer knowledge storage architecture, a three-level maturity system, and how workflows serve knowledge accumulation.

relatedArticles.title: Is Your Skill Up to Standard?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article proposes an 8-dimensional quantitative evaluation framework for AI Agent Skills, covering metrics such as metadata quality, execution guidance, and domain knowledge density to assign ratings, and designs a multi-model cross-validation process and four execution strategies to enhance the reliability and compatibility of the assessment.

relatedArticles.title: Data-Driven: 66.87% Bug Density Reduction in 10 Weeks of AI CR (Xiao Ma Ge) Implementation at Tieba
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: The Tieba Server team shared their complete 10-week practice of scaling Xiao Ma Ge AI CR, using rule customization, automated evaluation, and a three-layer feedback loop to increase review coverage from 33% to 84% and reduce bug density by 66.87%.

relatedArticles.title: After Reading the Claude Code Source Code, I Realized: The Differences Between Skills, MCP, and Rules Are Not as Big as You Think
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article, through an in-depth analysis of the leaked Claude Code source code, reveals the underlying implementation mechanisms of the three concepts—Rules, MCP, and Skills—pointing out that their core difference lies in where information is injected within the API request, and provides practical advice based on insights from the source code.
